claims.text: The proposed pipeline will simulate phonon heat conduction with an on-the-fly machine-learned force field and Green–Kubo molecular dynamics, while calculating electronic conductivity separately with DFT-based Boltzmann transport.
The decoupled pipeline will predict total thermal conductivity in HfNbTaTiZr significantly more accurately than earlier analytical models.
A nearly oxygen-free HfNbTaTiZr sample can represent an ideal, defect-free state.
An already-characterized HfNbTaTiZr specimen containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen provides a high-temperature thermal-conductivity benchmark.
Machine-learned interatomic potentials can capture atomic-scale mass and force-constant disorder sufficiently for Green–Kubo phonon-transport prediction in HfNbTaTiZr.
DFT-based Boltzmann transport can provide the electronic thermal-conductivity channel separately for HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed pipeline does not impose a typical Debye-temperature approximation.
Force-constant fluctuations are a dominant source of phonon scattering in the HEA discussed by the cited vibrational study.
Separately representing force-constant disorder and electronic band-structure effects will overcome limitations of previous analytical approximations.
Previous analytical approaches conflated lattice and electronic thermal conduction.
Earlier models commonly used a single Debye temperature to parameterize both lattice and electronic transport.
Decoupling phonon and electronic dynamics will reduce thermal-conductivity prediction error by roughly a factor of two.
Earlier-model errors exceed 50%, whereas the new approach should achieve errors of about ±15%.
Below 200 K, lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions in oxygen-free HfNbTaTiZr should be comparable.
Between 300 and 1200 K, an approximately 1 wt.% oxygen HfNbTaTiZr specimen has total thermal conductivity in the range 10–17 W/(K·m).
For the oxygen-containing specimen from 300 to 1200 K, the summed lattice-plus-electronic prediction will be within ±15% of experiment.
Oxygen contamination in powder-metallurgy HfNbTaTiZr can prevent formation of a single-phase random solid solution.

The prediction is limited to oxygen-minimized HfNbTaTiZr below 200 K and approximately 1 wt.% oxygen specimens from 300 to 1200 K; substantially different oxygen levels and phase inhomogeneity are outside scope.
Prediction accuracy may vary with machine-learning force-field training parameters, DFT settings, and unmodeled minor defect states.
A magnetic-field or magneto-thermal experiment can separate or suppress the electronic thermal-conductivity contribution below 200 K.

contradictions.description: Reducing error from greater than 50% to about 15% is an improvement of more than 3.3-fold in relative-error magnitude, not the stated roughly twofold reduction.

The simulations are described as using near-zero oxygen, but their summed output is directly required to predict measurements from a 1 wt.% oxygen specimen. No oxygen-containing simulation or correction is specified, despite oxygen level being treated as an applicability boundary.

The initial state is broadly described as single-phase while the approximately 1 wt.% oxygen control is included in scope; elsewhere phase inhomogeneity is excluded, although the cited HfNbTaTiZr evidence says oxygen contamination can prevent a single-phase random solid solution.
